newsitem.title: USA: Hartford officers arrested in alleged video beating.
newsitem.headline: Hartford officers arrested in alleged video beating.

text.p: Three Hartford police officers were arrested Friday in an investigation of the alleged beating of a Massachusetts motorist that was recorded on videotape, authorities said.

Officers Michael Ancona and Jacqueline Middleton were charged with second-degree assault and falsifying evidence in the Feb. 14 incident. A third officer, Hugh O'Callaghan, was charged only with falsifying a police report.

All three were suspended without pay until the matter is resolved in court or through administrative procedures, Bloomfield Police Chief Richard Mulhall told a news conference. They were released on a written promise to appear in court next week, Hartford State's Attorney Jim Thomas said.
Thomas declined to comment on the strength of his case. He said the 10-second videotape will not be made public unless it is eventually used in court.
"Certainly they are not above the law and they are being prosecuted to the full extent," Hartford Police Chief Joseph Croughwell said. But he called the matter "an isolated incident."
The Hartford and Bloomfield police departments conducted separate investigations of the incident, which was recoreded by a camera in a Bloomfield police cruiser.
Attorneys for all three officers said their clients did nothing wrong.

The victim of the alleged beating, James Wilson of Southwick, Massachusetts, pleaded not guilty in Hartford Thursday to four traffic violations related to the police chase through Hartford and Bloomfield that preceded his injuries.
The 37-year-old diesel mechanic said he was beaten by Hartford police officers after stepping away from his car and being ordered to lie on the ground.
